context: Dual-axis time series data visualization showing daily temperature (line) and weekly rainfall (bars) over 18 months, with explicit gap-handling techniques: dashed bridges, hatched bars, shaded regions, and a broken-axis zigzag indicator.
first_impression: Polished and information-dense, with deliberate color coding between the two axes and thoughtful gap annotation that elevates it well above a generic dual-axis chart.
what_works: The Tol palette (blue/cyan split between axes) is a genuine design choice — the color-coded axes, labels, and legend items create a coherent visual system where each data series owns its color throughout. The gap-handling vocabulary (dashed bridge, rose boundary circles, hatched bars, labeled gap callouts) is varied and readable without feeling cluttered.
what_doesnt: The right-axis label ('Weekly Rainfall (mm)') uses a rotated transform that positions it far outside the viewport — it's clipped and invisible in the rendered output, leaving the right axis unlabeled. The subtitle text is very small (12px, #888) and cramped between the title and legend row, making the annotation key hard to read at a glance.
